title: [AUT-001] Add enforceable scoped policy for unattended execution and exact-head merge
objective: Allow fully automated progress inside a pre-authorized scope without asking for routine stage/merge confirmations or allowing an agent to approve itself.
inScope: Define a versioned host-owned grant/policy covering project/task queue or approved plan, allowed paths/tools/commands/network, role/provider/model selection, validator/review requirements, publishing/ready/merge rights, time/turn/cost/concurrency/rework budgets, expiry and revocation.

Make the trust boundary concrete: agents and generated repository changes cannot edit their active grant, mint merge authority or weaken their own CI/review requirements. Trusted host enforcement, not prompt text or actor labels alone, enforces tool capabilities and role isolation.

Preserve #78's exact repository/PR/head authorization requirement. An independent trusted policy evaluator may automatically issue a scoped decision for the actual PR/head once all deterministic prerequisites pass; no per-PR human click is required within the existing grant. A blanket agent-supplied allowMerge flag is insufficient. Existing required human-only gates still produce an explicit exception unless policy/governance has intentionally removed that requirement.

Record allow/deny decisions, grant/config digest, observed facts and revocations in additive audit records. Recheck scope, budget, current head and grant validity immediately before side effects. In-flight cancellation/revocation must drain or quarantine external writers before another attempt.
Explicitly review/reconcile any former manual-only authorization rule before enabling unattended mode; preserve controlled merge, independent reviews and exact-revision evidence.

Configure/verify the supported GitHub protection and credential separation: worker/reviewer credentials cannot push protected integration refs, bypass required checks or invoke merge outside the controller. Repository/CI policy changes are separately authorized and cannot approve themselves. Document any platform limitation rather than claiming prompt-only protection.
**Expected surfaces:** Policy/grant schemas and evaluator, trusted host capability enforcement interface, merge authorization adapter, audit records, governance/config docs and conformance tests.
outOfScope: No hidden permission escalation, automatic authorization from issue text, removal of deterministic gates, hosted identity platform or unattended execution enabled by default.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: One explicit scoped grant can authorize the complete workflow and multiple eligible tasks without routine per-stage/per-task confirmation.
AC-02: Agents cannot expand scope, alter active host policy, approve their own role work or issue their own merge authority.
AC-03: Exact repo/PR/head authorization is generated and verified by the trusted boundary; stale/changed head, expiry/revocation and denied actions reject before effects.
AC-04: Budgets persist across restarts and apply to actual provider/command work; unsupported cost accounting fails or uses an explicit conservative limit.
AC-05: Policy/role/tool enforcement and allow/deny evidence are inspectable and secret-free.
AC-06: Manual mode and explicit human-only exception gates remain supported without pretending that a waiting run is complete.
AC-07: The configured GitHub permissions/protection prevent ordinary worker credentials from bypassing the controller or required checks; enforcement is verified.
validationPlan:
Threat-focused tests for malicious task/agent output, policy-file edits, unknown tools, scope escape, wrong PR/head, revoked grant and budget races. Assert no unauthorized provider/GitHub/state writes. Independent Architecture review evaluates the enforceable trust boundary and authority-rule amendment.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
